description: This case study is the California Public Utilities Commission's Aliso Canyon well failure page and the root cause analysis it hosts, covering the leak at the natural gas storage well SS-25 in the Santa Susana Mountains, found by SoCalGas crews on 23 October 2015 and stopped on 12 February 2016. The page describes the reopening of the facility on 19 July 2017 at reduced capacity, with the storage inventory now capped at 68.6 billion cubic feet compared with 86 before the leak, and links to the Blade Energy Partners root cause analysis released on 17 May 2019 as a main report with four supplementary volumes on approach, the SS-25 failure causes, post-leak events and casing integrity. Search-result summaries of the Blade report say the immediate cause was microbial corrosion of the outer casing and that SoCalGas lacked well integrity risk assessment. Access: free PDFs on the CPUC site; no licence is stated. Coverage is one storage facility. Caveats: the report itself was not opened, so the cause statements come from search summaries. It suits resilience and capacity planning studies of gas storage reliability, and it relates to the CPUC Aliso Canyon investigation record catalogued here as case_study-aliso-canyon-well-failure-cpuc-investigation.

outcomes: The leak at the largest natural gas storage facility in California was found on 23 October 2015 and stopped on 12 February 2016, and the well was sealed on 15 February 2016. The facility was reopened in 2017 at reduced capacity, with the storage inventory limit set at 68.6 billion cubic feet against 86 before the leak. Search-result summaries of the Blade root cause analysis report microbial corrosion of the well casing and no systematic well integrity risk assessment.
